text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT P0 - Elevated 5xx and timeouts observed from model-runner-prod since ~12:03 UTC. Auto-alerting SRE oncall. Link: https://internal.ops/incidents/1791112222
jenna (oncall): seeing a big spike in 5xx and gateway timeouts across the inference gateway, routing failures to model-runner-prod clusters.
kai (sre): any obvious memory/ooms in logs yet? can you grab recent pod logs for model-runner?
maria (eng-runtime): pulling logs now. One runner pod shows repeated "Segmentation fault (core dumped)" followed by OOM-kill for process "model-runner". Suspect kernel-level crash on NVidia driver or bad kernel module.
maria (eng-runtime): logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T12:02:47Z] model-runner[pid=4521] ERROR: kv-cache allocate failed: cannot allocate 512MB
[2026-03-15T12:02:48Z] model-runner[pid=4521] INFO: starting inference for request id=rx-9a3
[2026-03-15T12:02:48Z] model-runner[pid=4521] CRASH: Segmentation fault (core dumped)
[2026-03-15T12:02:48Z] kernel: kill process 4521 (model-runner) score 987 or sacrifice child
```
kai (sre): interesting - both OOM and segfault in same window. Could be a memory corruption when KV cache grows past threshold. Which model was being served on that pod?
maria (eng-runtime): model-tag: redwood-llm-xl-8k (quantized). traffic shows long-context requests (>= 6k tokens) spiked from a small set of customers.
sam (support): we already have 3 customers reporting degraded responses and errors. Two are on Dedicated, one hosted. I started a support thread and DM'd account teams.
jenna (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) reduce maximum context allowed at gateway for heavyweight models, 2) route new requests to fallback smaller model variant with stricter kv limits, 3) cordon the node with repeated crashes, 4) restart affected pods after patch flags. doing steps in parallel.
kai (sre): agree. I'd add temporary concurrency limit on model-runner group and disable KV prefetch. Maria, can you build a runtime flag to cap KV cache to 1Gi and toggle via config map?
maria (eng-runtime): yes. pushing a safe toggle to config: set MODEL_RUNNER_KV_MAX=1024MB and MODEL_PREFETCH=false. will roll to canary first.
jenna (oncall): applying gateway rule to route 40% traffic to fallback model now. command:
```
# route 40% of traffic for model redwood-llm-xl-8k -> redwood-llm-xl-8k-compact
rwctl route update --model redwood-llm-xl-8k --split 60:40 --target redwood-llm-xl-8k-compact
```
ops-bot: route update accepted, rollout id=rb-1791112222-1
kai (sre): also limit concurrency on the autoscaler: set max_concurrency=4 for model-runner deployment to reduce memory pressure.
jenna (oncall): applying concurrency limit with kubectl patch now.
```
kubectl -n prod patch deployment model-runner --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/limits","value":{"cpu":"4","memory":"8Gi"}}]'
```
maria (eng-runtime): configmap updated and canary rollout started to one pod.
ops-bot: canary pod model-runner-66a7 started with KV_MAX=1024MB MODEL_PREFETCH=false
maria (eng-runtime): canary looks stable for 30s, no segfaults. logs show KV allocations hitting cap and gracefully rejecting further prefetch.
jenna (oncall): I deleted the obviously crashed pod to let deployment recreate: `kubectl delete pod model-runner-7h2q` — new pod came up but then another crash observed on node node-12.
kai (sre): I'm leaning toward faulty GPU node or driver. Let's cordon node-12, drain workloads off it.
jenna (oncall): cordon + drain commands:
```
kubectl cordon node-12
kubectl drain node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
ops-bot: node-12 cordoned and drain initiated (evicting 6 pods). Notified k8s-scheduler.
sam (support): customer-facing status draft (for support and status page): "We are investigating elevated 500 errors for inference requests affecting a subset of long-context workloads. Mitigations in progress; some traffic has been routed to a smaller model variant to reduce errors. We'll post updates every 30 minutes."
jenna (oncall): sending that to status now. pinging account teams for Dedicated customers with long-context usage.
kai (sre): after cordon, no new crashes observed on remaining nodes for 10 minutes. evicted pods restarted on healthy nodes with new config. 5xx rate dropped from 12% to 1.8% — still above baseline but much improved.
maria (eng-runtime): opening a debug job to collect core dumps and run addr2line analysis. linking to runbook: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/model-crash
jenna (oncall): escalation decision: keep incident P0 until we confirm root cause. assigning incident lead to kai for handoff. I need to step out in 20m; kai you'll take over.
kai (sre): taking incident lead. action items: 1) keep fallback routing for at least 60m, 2) collect core dumps + driver logs from node-12, 3) run kernel and nvidia driver version check across nodes, 4) plan hotfix to reject extremely long-context requests at gateway if memory budget exceeded.
sam (support): I've notified affected customers and queued follow-ups. We've offered a rollback to prior model variant for Dedicated customers if needed.
ops-bot: scheduled cluster-wide agent to collect syslogs and nvidia-smi output: job id job-1791112222-collect
maria (eng-runtime): initial addr2line suggests crash inside attention kernel extension (gpu_attention.c:line 473). sending patch to runtime that adds bounds checks and falls back to CPU attention for pathological sequence lengths.
kai (sre): good. after that patch we can roll to canary and then wide. prefer to keep traffic split until patch is validated.
jenna (oncall): thanks team. handing to kai. I'll update the incident timeline and prepare handoff notes to postmortem doc.
kai (sre): received. I'll coordinate postmortem and link to this thread. current status: mitigation in place, partial customer impact, collecting artifacts. next update in 30m. :thumbsup:
